text:
maria: Heads up — since the compile change landed this morning I'm seeing a 90th percentile token latency spike on prod-gpu-pool-2. Anyone else?
ken: Yea noticed it around 06:10 UTC. Dashboard shows a sudden shift in kernel timeline — memcpy_32B kernels taking much more time.
sasha: grabbing nsys trace now for one of the hot requests. reproducer: send a 6k token chat with batch_size=1 and kv_cache enabled.
tracing-bot: nsys trace uploaded: https://perf-storage.internal/trace/1912345678/nsys_trace_006.zip (54MB)
maria: quick diff between before/after: KV cache lookups per request increased from 18 -> 62, eviction_rate up 3.2x. suspect cache invalidation on compilation artifacts.
ken: here's the nsys timeline snippet I pulled:```TIMELINE
0ms - conv_forward
1.2ms - memcpy small
1.5ms - attention_kv_load
2.8ms - attention_mm
4.0ms - memcpy small (spike)
```
sasha: nvprof flame shows a new kernel "select_kernel_variant" appears and dominates 35% of GPU time. That call wasn't present earlier. Looks like runtime now probes kernel variants at launch and sometimes falls back per-request.
maria: commit that touched selector: runtime/compile: allow lazy kernel probe (0f3a7d1). Could be the cause.
ken: I ran perfetto on a before snapshot and after snapshot. Before: continuous attention kernels, memcpy amortized 4%. After: many short memcpy interrupts between kernels. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/ui/trace/1912345678
ops-elena: any quick mitigation? Canary rollback?
sasha: short-term: pin to model-variant v1.2 which bypasses probe path, that removes the select_kernel_variant calls. I tested on staging, 95th goes back down.
maria: good. For postmortem we should: 1) capture full nsys for 10 requests before rolling back 2) run kernel selector in isolation with microbenchmarks to reproduce 3) add a sampling flag to avoid per-request probing 4) add an eval that measures memcpy small percentage.
ken: I'm starting a bisect run to find minimal commit (will post sha). running a scripted workload:```bash
./tools/loadtest --seed 42 --batch 1 --seq 6k --kv on --duration 5m --trace nsys
```
maria: note to self: check whether KV cache TTL/ID changed in same PR set — might be double invalidation: compile change + cache key format tweak.
sasha: attaching quick grep of selector code:```c
if (!kernel_variant_cached()) {
  probe_kernel_variant(); // does a tiny launch and memcpy roundtrip
  cache_variant();
}
```
ken: probe_kernel_variant triggers a tiny memcpy to check compatibility on the device — that's the memcpy small we see. On heavy traffic it happens often because cache misses are high.
ops-elena: For rollout plan: revert the compile probe, or gate it behind a feature flag and default off for Dedicated nodes.
maria: agreed. I'll open a PR to gate the probe and add metrics for probe_count per node.
sasha: also adding a perf regression test to CI: run small microbench that asserts memcpy_fraction < 8%.
ken: update: bisect found the commit stack — the probe change landed with a cache-key refactor around 0f3a7d1 -> 1b9c4e2. Marking both for rollback candidate.
maria: thanks. After we revert/gate, we should schedule a follow-up to redesign probe to be async and amortized across nodes.
ops-elena: rolling back the probe on prod now (starting canary). will monitor traces. :rocket: 
tracing-bot: canary rollback deployed to 10% traffic at 07:48 UTC. will collect nsys samples for 5m.
ken: post-rollback quick check: memcpy small dropped back to baseline, KV eviction back to normal. looks fixed on canary.
maria: great. save traces and close the loop in the PR description with before/after perfetto links and the nsys zips.
sasha: I'll draft the incident note with timeline and root cause: 'eager per-request kernel probe + increased KV cache misses => memcpy spike and latency regression'.
maria: perfect. Thanks all.
